Danny Serrano, AICP

From: Daniel Serrano <Daniel@lesardevelopment.com <mailto:Daniel@lesardevelopment.com> >
Sent: Wednesday, May 31, 2023 7:50:48 AM
To: Monica Hernandez <monicah@casafamiliar.org <mailto:monicah@casafamiliar.org> >
Cc: Ruiz, Elise <Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov <mailto:Elise.Ruiz@sdcounty.ca.gov> >
Subject: RE: Regional Water Equity Report - Affordable Housing Connection

Dear Monica Hernandez,

I hope you are well.  I’m working as a consultant with LeSar Development Consultants for the County of San Diego to identify ways in which to incentivize affordable housing to utilize sustainable use/reuse of water and stormwater.  This research is part of the County’s anticipated Regional Water Equity Report (the attached fact sheet provides additional context) that will help to inform the County’s larger drought management and water sustainability practices to proactively address the challenges of our region’s reliance on water sources.

We’d like to invite you and others from Casa Familiar to participate in a one-hour (virtual) interview with LDC’s project team and County staff (Elise Ruiz/Group Program Manager with the County’s Land Use and Environment Group).  Our goal is to learn from your experiences in the affordable housing and water conservation/stormwater capture and reuse fields which will help us to identify ways in which to incentivize affordable housing to utilize water conservation/stormwater capture and reuse.  The interview would focus on stormwater infrastructure and affordable housing development process, the financial and regulatory barriers to implementing water and stormwater projects in housing, and potential opportunities to leverage better outcomes in both sectors.  Key themes from the interviews will be summarized in a brief memorandum to County staff.

Please let us know if you (and others from your team) would be willing to join us for a one-hour virtual interview.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

Danny Serrano, AICP

Daniel@lesardevelopment.com <mailto:Daniel@lesardevelopment.com>

619-850-1527

Subject: RE: OSEJ/RDF Steering Committee Agenda

Hi Murtaza and all -  great meeting on Friday and we received a lot of DCAO input and direction. I added the main action items below, based on Sarah’s feedback.

  1.  Regional Decarbonization Framework
     *   DCAO: we need to foster the business community as well as workforce. Wherever we talk about green jobs we need to talk about green industry. They go hand in hand.
                                                               i.      Murtaza need to follow up with David Flores - the items on green industry that Sarah shared was not included in Chairwoman's talking points
                                                             ii.      We need to highlight both -- it is not one or the other -- Sarah needs help reinforcing this piece with D1 (or else we will face obstacles in the business community.

     *   DCAO feedback on Symposium: Donna needs to be engaged on this -- she needs to take the lead on this. Sarah requests a meeting (30 min) to talk about the symposium
                                                               i.      We need to come back with Sarah on our plan to move forward, then have another call with David and other partners

     *   DCAO feedback on D3 convening: need to put a timeframe of when the convening needs to take place. If she can't make it then we need to move forward on it. Hold them to a timeline (because we need it for the BL, Board hearing, etc.). Can't have their district missing in this.
     *   DCAO question for us to consider: Because we are bringing this home through public health -- for purposes of when we go to the Board - should we tee up some joint Public Health approach/PPT for March hearing?
     *   DCAO: how many Playbook copies are we printing? Maybe print one for each Board office and our office -- like 30 or 40
     *   DCAO: Sarah wants information as the comments come in on the Playbook -- we may not include things proactively -- but have them discuss in the public setting
  1.  Regional Equity Group
     *   For when Murakawa meets with Sarah: how do we ensure all of our communities are represented? Not just cities, but unincorporated as well. Who will they engage? Who are the players for the
                                                               i.      What info do we need to provide them so they are educated about San Diego region dynamics -- this will be important
                                                             ii.      Connect Murakawa with PDS EJ team

  1.  Regional Water Equity Project
     *   DCAO: always Board office that moves a Board letter forward - they should be in the know. But also the whole Board took action. Start with key Board office, and then say that we are going to share with all office because we need to meet the needs. Different Board offices will have different perspectives of this -- like all the ag and Borrego Springs (worst groundwater impacted in the State) -- they have critical needs.
                                                               i.      For the one pager -- who needs to weigh in, in additional to the Board offices -- Donna, Michael. Need people far removed to review and provide insight

     *   DCAO: would like a timeline on all aspects of outreach, when will we start to make the pitch - before it starts
  1.  Misc.
     *   DCAO briefing request: would like a briefing on Spring Valley communities in terms of what we are doing for TCC grant.
                                                               i.      How are PDS and DPW involved in these conversations
                                                             ii.      As we are moving forward on SLTF -- what is the alignment, what is the overlap
                                                           iii.      Anything related to road planning, housing planning
                                                           iv.      How are we pulling this all together globally
                                                             v.      How is the work we are doing as part of TCC -- into the parcel by parcel analysis and SLUF

Rebeca Appel

Hi Stephanie,

The Task 3.B deliverable is on Sharepoint in the Task 3.B folder <https://projectsitesb.geosyntec.com/8/SW033129-0547/_layouts/15/start.aspx#/SitePages/Home.aspx?RootFolder=%2F8%2FSW033129-0547%2FShared%20Documents%2FTask%203%20-%20SW%20Capture%20and%20Use%20at%20County%20Parks%20and%20Facilities%2FTask%203B%20Deliverable&FolderCTID=0x012000BB8DC2F928EF0944BBEB156EFA200989&View=%7B09ED6256-943F-4252-81B3-27AB4979A7B9%7D> . As discussed on the call today, the table presents the attributes associated with each County facility, supporting the potential infiltration and diversion screening as well as the next Task 3.C's prioritization and identification of potential project opportunities. These facilities are compiled from the Task 3.A deliverable and include the additional facilities you sent on 7/3 from the missing data we identified during that task. The following two tabs are included for the Task 3.B deliverable:

*	Attributes, Rationale, and Desc: This tab provides the rationale, sources, and description of the various attributes added to each facility.
*	FAC_INF_DIV_CAP_RESULTS: This tab provides the attribute results for each facility, along with the infiltration and diversion screening results. The initial screening criteria for feasible infiltration and diversion for water supply in Columns O and P are listed below. Onsite Capture and Use screening will be shown during Task 3.C. Additionally, we have included if the parcel overlaps with a SWCFS Parcel, has dry weather flows at MS4 outfalls within 500ft sourced from WSP, and has water demands based on the data provided by the County in May.

Task 3.C will identify the potential project opportunities based on additional applied criteria to rule out areas not ideal for infiltration, diversion, or onsite capture and use (e.g., not within 40ft of septic parcels or 100ft of contamination sites, already has recycled water etc.). and include the weights and resulting scores for each of the facilities along with the prioritized list based on the prioritization framework.

It would be helpful to know if you would like us to remove leased facilities or if there are any other facilities we should remove prior to the prioritization and identification of potential project opportunities. Additionally, let us know if you would like us to include any other attributes for these facilities to support Task 3.C. Please provide this information by July 21 if possible.

1.	Infiltration

	a.	Infiltration screening

		*	Groundwater basins within 1-mile buffer, or;
		*	Within 1-Mile of a drinking well, but outside 150 feet of a drinking well, and;
		*	Permeable geology (Alluvium, Basalt, Conglomerate, Sandstone), and;
		*	Slopes <15%.

2.	Diversion

	a.	Diversion screening

		*	Within sewershed to recycled water treatment plant

Please let us know if you have questions!

Thank you!

Now, more than ever, the work in the stormwater management field is critical to achieving a more resilient future. Collectively, our actions can lead to a Rain Ready California. What does that look like? Investing in our communities to reconnect the hydrologic cycle (e.g., stormwater capture). Rethinking how we work to integrate across water sectors to achieve our shared common goals. Protecting our waterways through true source control and effective BMPs. Engaging within the stormwater profession and the communities we serve to communicate that stormwater is a resource. Advocating for funding, regulations, and legislation to support these outcomes. Updated request scope as of 5/17/24 refinement sent by Mr.Small:

We have put some thought into search restrictions and terms and here is what we would suggest:

(1) total time range of January 1, 2023 through July 31, 2023
(2) Anything that includes Juli Beth Hinds, Dr. Amy Lerner, urban studies and planning (USP), global policy & strategy (GPS), UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms
(3) Anything related to the regional water equity report or RDF
(4) Anything containing a reference to "Juli Beth Hinds, Dr Amy Lerner,  Geosyntec, USP, GPS, or the RWER or RDF", UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms sent to or from "Elise Ruiz, anyone at Murakawa Communications, anyone at Geosyntec including but not limited to Ken Susillo, Megan Otto, Stephanie Zinn; and anyone at the County including but not limited to Stephanie Gaines, Crystal Benham, Todd Snyder, Sarah Agassi, Eden Brukman, and Murtaza Baxamusa"

Original Request:

To Whom it may Concern:
I am writing on behalf of my client Juli Beth Hinds. On behalf of Ms. Hinds, please consider this a formal request pursuant to California Public Records Act, Government Code §6250 et seq. for copies of all DOCUMENTS of the County of San Diego Land Use & Environment Group that reference or relate to: Juli Beth Hinds; the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at the University of California San Diego; or Nathan Fletcher. ("DOCUMENTS" as used herein, shall be defined to mean any ''writing'' as that term is defined in Evidence Code section 250, including, but not limited to, correspondence, emails, texts, communications of any kind, recordings, tapes, computer print-outs, records, slides, photographs, notes, working papers, written analyses, memoranda, plans, telegraphs, telexes and transcriptions, electronic data, and notes or memoranda made by any telephone communications.) This request encompasses all DOCUMENTS dated or created between the dates of January 1, 2022 through the date of this letter.
I request delivery of these records to our firm's office, located at 402 W. Broadway, Suite 1270, San Diego, CA 92101, or we can arrange to pick them up at a reasonable location designated by the County.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
